content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: The practical goal of calculating totals and averages is to produce a result set whose meaning is clear. Confirm which rows enter the query, how values are transformed or combined, and whether NULLs, duplicates, ties, or one-to-many relationships change the output.

items.title: Correct handling of empty input and NULL values
items.text: Correct handling of empty input and NULL values requires deliberate handling of absent or unknown values. In SQL, NULL is not the same as zero or an empty string; use IS NULL / IS NOT NULL for direct tests and check how expressions and aggregates propagate unknowns.

content_blocks.code:
SELECT c.name AS category, COUNT(p.product_id) AS product_count,
       COALESCE(SUM(p.stock_quantity), 0) AS units_in_stock,
       ROUND(AVG(p.price), 2) AS average_price
FROM categories AS c
LEFT JOIN products AS p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
HAVING COUNT(p.product_id) >= 0
ORDER BY c.name;
content_blocks.expected_output: The report returns one row per category, including empty categories because of the LEFT JOIN. COUNT(product_id) ignores unmatched NULL product IDs.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a query is correct because it returns some rows.
common_mistakes.why: A result can omit valid records, multiply joined rows, mishandle NULLs, or rely on a non-deterministic order.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected row grain, add targeted edge cases, and use a stable tie-breaker whenever order or pagination matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying PostgreSQL syntax into another SQL engine without checking support.
common_mistakes.why: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, and Oracle differ in types, functions, row limits, procedural features, and transaction behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Label the target engine/version and verify the relevant official reference before adapting the query.
